correctness.rationale: The frozen counts were not false. The final repair at /workspace/repairs/5/RESULT.md and /workspace/repairs/5/SLOGAN.txt instead makes the complete orbit-level classification its claim and provides all 19 rows. Independently ran /workspace/branches/replay_order16.py without running any uploaded checker. It enumerates all 6,907 anchored candidates via difference disjointness at reciprocal sizes, keeping exactly 715. It intersects exact Gaussian-integer Fourier zeros over every normalized complement, checks every listed spectrum, and counts all subgroups of the required sizes by closure under differences (numbers of subgroups by ambient order 1,2,4,8,16 are 1,3,7,3,1). A nonzero difference intersection is exactly a repeated sum; with 16 sums disjointness implies a tiling. Normalizing a complement does not change its Fourier zeros; the cardinality and difference condition for a witness give an orthogonal basis simultaneously on all complements, not just a representative complement. The 96 invertible linear maps are exactly the generator-image pairs independent modulo 2, with four lifts per image. All normalized affine images of the 19 representatives are disjoint between rows and their union equals the independently computed tile set. The spectral transport M^(-T) preserves the subgroup property. The replay verified every orbit size, complement count, frequency witness and subgroup count, including obstruction orbit totals by size (0,1,4,5,0). The repaired printed table was checked row-for-row against the independently replayed witness data; the aggregate labelled obstruction profile (0,96,352,720,0) follows from the verified anchored totals by the factor 16/k. The unchanged uploaded verification files were inspected as evidence, not run. Only this finite group is covered.

value.rationale: The repaired result is a finite classification of a natural simultaneous-basis invariant modulo the full group of symmetries. Given any tile one can identify its orbit, recover a single basis for every complement, and tell not only whether a subgroup choice is possible but how many subgroups qualify. The per-class distinctions and concrete witnesses are useful beyond the aggregate, which cannot identify them. Neither publishing the known counts again nor adding a certificate for them alone would suffice.
